packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 16 - BLIND IMAGE READING (unverified)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading for this packet. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..006.jpg. I listed the packet directory with ls to get the image filenames, and I made enlarged, contrast-enhanced copies (grayscale and colour) of some areas in work/zoom16/ (a.png, a2.png, b.png, b2.png, c.png, c2.png, d.png, d2.png, e2.png). I did nothing beyond the rules.

All six images loaded.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001: overview of one side of a vertical parchment strip, about 5 cm wide and 14-15 cm tall against the ruler. It is cut from a column: the right edge runs along a vertical ruling or column edge, and the left edge is cut irregularly through the text. About 30 lines of small gothic textura in brown/black ink. Many small black holes and losses, probably adhesive or insect damage.
- At upper left there is a large initial in red and blue/grey with pen-flourish (red penwork scrolls running up into the upper margin). It is about 4 lines deep and the text beside it is indented. The upper margin above the text block is blank apart from the flourish.
- Near the bottom (image-003 lines ~13-16) there are lines in red ink: a rubric, mixed with or followed by a line or two of brown text, then the lower margin. This looks like a rubric (heading) between sections. My interpretation is a closing or opening rubric before a new section.
- image-004: overview of the other side of the same strip (mirror shape, ruler again). Same script, about 30 lines. Upper margin shows faint offset or show-through. In the upper right (image-005 lines 1-4) there is a faint, partly lost initial in grey/red, about 3-4 lines deep, with indented text. Mid-column (image-005 ~line 9) a small red initial or paraph. Near the bottom (image-006 lines ~11-12) there are two lines in red: a rubric. Below that is one brown line, then red ruling/stroke(s) and the lower margin.
- I see no running titles, interlinear glosses or marginal notes. I cannot see underlining. There is only one column, cut on the left; the strip does not show the full column width, so every line is truncated on at least one side.
- Overlaps: image-002 (top) and image-003 (bottom) are native tiles of image-001; image-003 lines 1-4 repeat image-002's last lines. image-005 and image-006 are tiles of image-004; image-006 lines 1-2 repeat image-005's bottom lines.

SELECTED SPANS
I picked the red rubric lines on both sides, which are the most legible, plus a few brown lines next to them. The brown text body is very abraded and smudged, with ink bleeding into the parchment grain. Even at 2x enlargement with contrast boost, I could not securely read connected words in the main text. I give only isolated tentative forms below. Everything else is unread.

SIDE A (image-001 / tiles image-002, image-003)

image-003, rubric area (counted from top of image-003; red ink unless noted):
l.13 (red)  Qu(od)? (est)? a? [illegible] ...ue? ... p(ri)ma? / punct? [illegible] Ca[...] (the final "Ca" is red, at the right edge, cut)
l.14 (red)  ...dient? / ...cient? longanimi? / longani(m)? [illegible] ... meti? / mens? : Si? / Ai? [cut]
l.15 (brown with red at left?)  [illegible] ..., ... (uncertain "... fecit? em? ..." ) ... tua? / trad? . Ca? / Ce? [cut]
l.16 (mixed red/brown, very faded)  [illegible] ... (some letters only: "...iuntu? ... ras? ..." ) [illegible]
Remarks: these are the readable letter shapes only. The words are not secure, and I cannot fix the rubric's sense. Line 13 opens with a large-ish "Qu" in red. The red "Ca"/"Ce" at the right ends of l.13 and l.15 may start capitals of following sentences or headings, but I am not sure.

image-002, brown text beside and below initial (lines counted from top of image-002; first text line = l.1 at about y=200):
l.1-4: text indented right of the initial. [illegible]
l.5 (y~410)  ...?ilar? ... d(ic)i? ... [illegible] ... (an apparent "... ex? ..." mid-line) [illegible]
l.6-9  [illegible]
l.10 (y~640)  ...tatus . si? / sic? ... [illegible] ... aput? / apud? ... [illegible]
l.11 (y~690)  (red letter(s) mid-line, possibly a red paraph or "L") ... [illegible]
Rest of image-002/003 brown text: unread or illegible.

SIDE B (image-004 / tiles image-005, image-006)

image-006, rubric (counted from top of image-006):
l.12 (red)  [cut]...phis? / ...ohis? C?ri?sostomi? / Clisostomi? de repa(ra)c(i)o(n)e? / reparac(ion)e? [cut?]
l.13 (red)  [cut]...ber? / ...bet? p(ri)mus? / p(re)mus? eiusd(em)? / eiusde(m)? de p(...)? / ps(a)lmo? / p(re)lato? [cut]
l.14 (brown)  [illegible] ... [illegible] (no secure words)
below: red horizontal pen strokes, then the lower margin
Remarks: l.12-13 are the clearest text on the fragment. The letter sequence in l.12 looks like "...sostomi" (or "-stomum"), preceded by a letter that may be C, Cr or Cl. Next comes "de repa" + abbreviation; the final word could be "reparac(ion)e" or "repara(tion)e". In l.13 "p(ri)mus" (p with an abbreviation stroke) and "eiusd(em)" (with a suspension mark) are fairly likely. The last word starts with p and has an abbreviation, so I cannot tell between "psalmo", "p(re)lato" and others. The first word of l.13 is cut ("...ber"/"...bet"); "liber" is possible but not visible.

image-005 brown text (lines from top; first text line l.1 at about y=200):
l.1-3: beside the faint initial at right. [illegible]
l.4 (y~380)  ...n? enuidia? ... [illegible] ... (a point) . Sed? / Et? in? [illegible]
l.5 (y~430)  ...tu(m)? ... [illegible] ... et? / tunc? ... [illegible]
l.6-8  [illegible]
l.9 (y~700) a red initial (possibly "A" or "T") inside the line, with damage; text before and after [illegible]
Rest of image-005/006 brown text: unread or illegible.

LIMITATIONS
- This is a narrow strip cut from a single column, so every line is truncated. I cannot rebuild word breaks at the cut edge.
- The brown ink of the main text is heavily abraded and blurred. There are many holes and losses (black spots). My readings of the brown text are fragmentary and not reliable enough for a source match on their own.
- The red rubrics (image-006 l.12-13; image-003 l.13-14) are the best anchors, but even these are tentative letter-by-letter readings.
- I cannot tell from these images which side is recto or verso.
- A higher-resolution capture, multispectral imaging or raking light might recover the brown text, especially the lines next to the rubrics. A wider view showing the conjoint or adjacent fragments would also help.
